summary:
Constructed shared accessibility/source/fixed-point laws and separate efficient, typed-motion, fact-grounding, explanatory-antecedent, strict-parthood and all-premise warrant transfers. Rejected identifying heterogeneous PSR reasons/facts with one-level regress, unary warrant paths with sufficient justification, fixed-point equality with accessibility, or absent warrant with causal impossibility. The common infinite graph admits local all-on activity but no generated foundation warrant. No source interpretation was added and no root premise discharged; actual domain premises and the epistemic bridge remain open. Queried the landed finite-model library for FINITE-ANCESTRY-NO-LOOPS-PER-SE-NO-REGRESS using its complete three-premise set, reusing the same-head live verification of 48 models and 481 certificates. No registered model evaluates the requested target and full premise set together; this absence supplies no derivability, consistency or closure conclusion.

Lane F (#2103, 2026-11-27). Extracted the constructive no-return-path clause already used by Graph.controls_of_wellFounded. The typed application runs on ConcreteExistentialSupply.graph m w, with the same grounding relation, selected world and subtype of actual concreta as ActualGroundingWF. It supplies the acyclicity input of the selected-cone and occupant routes under the existing whole-actual-graph well-foundedness premise. The theorem has no inhabitant input or conclusion. The occupied successor profile in GroundedOccupantRegress has no cycles but an anchored descending chain, so the reverse implication fails. The only commitment made explicit is that acyclicity follows when the existing well-foundedness premise is adopted. Removed unrelated frame, modal existence, roothood and population definition links from the well-foundedness statement after checking its Lean body. This scope correction exposed carried metadata in dependent argument records. Other components of the regress package have their separately recorded domains and application boundaries.
